examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_{1}^{3}(x+2)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}+2x\right]_{1}^{3}\\&=\left(\frac{9}{2}+6\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}+2\right)\\&=8\end{aligned}$

The shaded region has area $8$ square units.

Expand the square and write the reciprocal term using a negative power.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_{1}^{3}\left(x+\frac{3}{x}\right)^{2}\,dx\\&=\int_{1}^{3}(x^{2}+6+9x^{-2})\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^{3}}{3}+6x-\frac{9}{x}\right]_{1}^{3}\\&=(9+18-3)-\left(\frac{1}{3}+6-9\right)\\&=24-\left(-\frac{8}{3}\right)\\&=\frac{80}{3}\end{aligned}$

coverage.summary: Authored five examples covering all distinct assessed methods with changed source values. Each has separate editable question and solution fields, explicit endpoint substitution and appropriate equals gutters; independent equations have no phantom equals. Solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. The editable graph uses purposeful area shading, black marks and declared label sizes, with no answer annotations in the question. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither altered nor re-audited. Actual rendering and final-size typography remain for the later visual stage.

examples.derivation: A primitive is x²/2+2x. Endpoint subtraction gives 21/2−5/2=8. The graph shows y=x+2 with endpoint heights 3 and 5 over [1,3]; its shaded trapezium has area (3+5)×2/2=8. This follows the source example at lines 1098–1108 and image28.
Writing 9/x² as 9x⁻² gives primitive −9/x. Evaluation gives −9/6−(−9/3)=3/2. The integrand is continuous on [3,6]. This adapts Guided Practice part f at lines 1170–1174; no diagram is necessary.

Expansion gives x²+3x, with primitive x³/3+3x²/2. Evaluation from 0 to 2 gives 8/3+6=26/3. Expansion before integration follows lines 1128–1134 and Guided Practice part a at lines 1153–1162; no diagram is necessary.

The square expands to x²+6+9x⁻². A primitive is x³/3+6x−9/x. Its endpoint values are 24 and −8/3, giving 80/3. The interval excludes zero. This adapts Development question 13(a), lines 1403–1410; no diagram is necessary.
Endpoint evaluation gives k²+4k−5. Equating this to 16 gives k²+4k−21=(k+7)(k−3)=0. The roots are −7 and 3; k>0 selects 3. This adapts Development question 11(e), lines 1377–1390.
